items.basis: Electrostatic levitation cannot provide sufficient force density to support a proof mass against gravity and operational accelerations without requiring impractical voltage levels or electrode areas, as demonstrated by the fundamental limitations in capacitive force generation cited in doi:10.3390/mi9110602

The operating boundary requires maintaining force within electrostatic limits, but the candidate fails to address how the control system will handle sudden high-g shocks that exceed electrostatic restoring force capacity, creating an unavoidable failure mode that violates the boundary conditions

The provided evidence (doi:10.23919/ursi.2018.8406772) shows that electrostatic suspension systems in MEMS devices are inherently unstable without sophisticated feedback control, contradicting the candidate's claim of stable operation

The candidate predicts zero-g offset will remain below 50mg after shock, but provides no evidence that electrostatic levitation can match or improve upon the baseline performance of MEMS accelerometers which have demonstrated sub-5mg stability in commercial implementations

The sigma-delta modulator control system requires sampling rates far exceeding the mechanical resonance frequency of MEMS accelerometers, making real-time control implementation impossible with current MEMS fabrication processes as evidenced by the limitations in doi:10.1109/iic.2015.7150884

The testable prediction of zero-g offset remaining below 50mg fails to specify measurement methodology, temperature conditions, or long-term drift characteristics, making the claim unverifiable and potentially masking significant performance degradation that would still occur despite preventing contact stiction
